I called on Monday to ask about booking a blood test and was told to call back on Wednesday at 8am, which I did. The appointment was booked. On Friday, I called again just to double-check where the blood test would be done, and I was clearly told it would be done at the GP practice at 12:40. Based on this, I cancelled my plans and arranged my day around the appointment.

Then, at 4:48pm on Friday, I received a call from the practice. First a receptionist told me I apparently needed to see a doctor first. Then the phone was passed to another woman whose attitude was extremely rude and dismissive. She told me I cannot have the blood test because I’m “too young”, which is ridiculous as I am 24 years old. When I explained that the last time I had blood tests was when I was 12, she said it “doesn’t matter” because it wasn’t done with them — which makes absolutely no sense.

I explained I’m concerned about my health and that I feel like I might faint when getting out of bed. Instead of showing any care or reassurance, she interrogated me with “what are you concerned about?” in a tone that made me nervous and uncomfortable. She then said she would need to see me first to check my blood pressure  something that was never mentioned in any of the previous three phone calls.

The lack of communication is shocking, but what made this experience so upsetting was the dismissive and rude attitude. I was made to feel like I was wasting their time for simply wanting to check my health.
